overview: This bill turns the Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Pilot Program into a regular program and extends it. The program, run by the Treasury Department, lets the government pay rewards to people who provide information that helps find and recover stolen assets linked to foreign government corruption that are held in U.S. financial institutions. The bill drops "pilot" from its name, removes a three-year time limit, and keeps the program running for seven years after the bill becomes law. On November 4, 2025, the House Financial Services Committee reported it and it was placed on the House calendar for a floor vote.
for: Supporters say paying for tips helps the government track down money stolen by corrupt foreign officials and hidden in the U.S. financial system.
against: Critics say the bill extends the program for seven years without requiring a fresh review of how well the pilot has worked.
